column11: That lighting and windows play a lot bigger part than i expected
I discovered that I was more of a mood based person rather than each elements.

I cared more about the space and overall atmosphere of the image than the individual components. Some spaces had elements I really liked, but they didn’t have the atmosphere I was drawn to. I tend to prioritize atmosphere over details.
I thought I want a bright home office with light colors, but during the process I find myself don't really like pure white room but instead prefer brown/grey color.

My favorite style is sometimes not the style I would like to have in my own house. For example, I love having fluffy carpets and delicate decorations in the room, but if it's my own house, I worry about maintenance more than the visual entertainment, but if I see an Airbnb has similar decorations I would go for those styles as I wouldn't need to worry about cleaning.
The system captured successfully my preference of ambient light and warm color, and it help me discovered my hidden likes about dark brown-ish furniture and small room spaces.
column12: sometimes the gen model provides images that is too close-up to certain elements in the room. It would be great if the camera can be pulled back and show the whole view of the room.

column11: I just realized I am a huge fan of greenery and decorative plants. And for lighting - I never thought about the style or size of wall openings, but now i have a clear view of what the window should be designed in my living room.

I think the system learned that I like big windows with plenty of green plants in the view which is pretty good and I didn't think a lot of before. Also the system found out that I like tall ceilings.
I think the system learned that "inspiring" to me implies window and green plants
I thought I would like a layout where everything stayed on the same level.
I like earthen tones more
It made me realized more items or specific detail i want from visually seeing the images.
It gave me more visual idea of how contemplative bedroom looks like. I was't very sure either because my ideal bedroom would be not contemplative.
I liked how it started showing more curved edges (I liked that!) instead of minimal simple lines

I first thought about plants and natural light but actually for a bedroom to be cozy I realized that did not matter that much, its more about the bed a confy places to sit around, and textures (pillows, blankets). And also what make sit cozy for me besides that is the warm light and looking to the room and thinking I would be comfortable in it.
The system acknowledged my preference on living things/plants and adequately applied to the space
